subject: reasoning
question: Accordioning to the Indian Government how many Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs) were notified by the Government of India as of June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**34**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **June 2025**, the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** has notified a total of **34** **Khelo India State Centres of Excellence** (**KISCEs**) across **31 States and Union Territories** in **India**.
 
• The **KISCE** initiative is a flagship program under the **Khelo India Scheme**, aimed at upgrading existing sports infrastructure in **States** and **Union Territories** to a world-class standard.
 
• Each center is tasked with focusing on specific **Olympic sport disciplines** to ensure concentrated development of talent and resources, helping **India** improve its standing in the **Olympic Games**.
 
• The selection of these **34** centers is based on the quality of existing infrastructure, coaching facilities, and the performance history of the **State** in particular sports.
 
• Financial assistance is provided by the **Central Government** to these centers to cover recurring and non-recurring costs, including **sports science** support, high-performance coaches, and technical equipment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Khelo India Scheme**:
 
 
• Launched in the financial year **2017-18**, this umbrella scheme was introduced by the **Government of India** to revive the sports culture at the grassroots level.
 
• The scheme is divided into **12 verticals**, ranging from infrastructure development to talent identification and community coaching.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Objectives**:
 
 
• The primary goal of **KISCE** is to create a robust ecosystem for athletes who have moved past the introductory stage and are ready for high-performance training.
 
• By **June 2025**, the integration of **sports science** (including nutrition, physiotherapy, and psychology) has become a mandatory component of these centers to ensure the holistic development of athletes.
 
 
 
• **Identification of Talent**:
 
 
• Athletes for these centers are often identified through national competitions such as the **Khelo India Youth Games** and **Khelo India University Games**.
 
• Selected athletes receive a **scholarship** and access to **residential training facilities**, aiming for peak performance in the **2028** and **2032** **Olympic Games**.
 
 
 
• **Role of States and UTs**:
 
 
• While the **Central Government** provides the funding and technical guidelines, the day-to-day management of these **34** centers remains with the respective **State Governments** or **UT Administrations**.
 
• This collaborative model ensures that the development of sports is not centralized but spread across the diverse geography of **India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The number of **KISCEs** has seen a steady increase since the first batch was announced, reflecting the government's commitment to reaching a target of at least one center of excellence in every **State** and **UT**.
 
• The **Sports Authority of India** (**SAI**) acts as the monitoring agency for these centers, ensuring that the quality of training meets international benchmarks.
 
• Prominent sports included in the **KISCE** focus list are **Archery**, **Athletics**, **Boxing**, **Hockey**, **Shooting**, and **Weightlifting**.
